abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) are key mechanisms of regulating protein function, yet quantitative PTM data remain fragmented across publications, supplementary datasets, and specialized resources. Here, we present qPTM 3.0, an integrated resource for quantitative PTM dynamics and AI-assisted knowledge discovery. The current release contains 15 652 063 quantitative events on 994 878 modification sites within 49 280 proteins across 3988 conditions, curated from 846 publications and spanning 12 PTM types in human, mouse, rat, and yeast. Raw mass spectrometry (MS) data associated with the curated entries were re using MaxQuant, and each modification site was assigned a five-star reliability score. Detailed annotations of experimental context, protein information, functional regulation, regulators, and inhibitors are also provided. qPTM 3.0 further introduces two AI-assisted modules. The PTM research agent enables natural-language exploration of qPTM 3.0 and complementary resources by synthesizing evidence on PTM regulators, regulatory conditions, and functional consequences. The data collection agent supports database curation through automated literature screening, full-text retrieval, metadata extraction, quantitative table parsing, and raw MS data acquisition within a human-in-the-loop workflow. Together, these features support systematic exploration of quantitative PTM dynamics and evidence-based biological interpretation. The online service is freely available at https://qptm.omicsbio.info/.
